column1: # ERRATA.tsv -- corrections applied to upstream PSlibrary recipes.
# The recipe database is sliced verbatim out of the upstream .job files by
# tools/extract_pslibrary.sh, and "verbatim" is the point: it is what lets us
# say a deck is PSlibrary's and mean it.  A handful of upstream decks are
# nevertheless wrong in a way that makes ld1.x produce an unusable file.  Those
# are corrected here rather than by editing the extracted template, because an
# edited template is silently destroyed the next time anyone re-runs the
# extractor -- which is exactly what happened to the caesium recipe once
# already, leaving a correction on disk that no test and no changelog knew
# about.
# A row is only admissible when the upstream value is *impossible*, not merely
# unusual, and the correction is the minimal edit that removes the
# impossibility.  Anything that is a matter of taste stays as upstream wrote
# it.  Every row records what was measured, so the claim can be rechecked.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   set        recipe set, as named by the extractor (us-low, paw-high, ...)
#   element    element symbol
#   tag        variant tag (spnl.1.0.0, ...)
#   field      the input keyword corrected
#   upstream   the exact upstream text
#   corrected  the exact replacement text
#   reason     why upstream cannot be right, and what was measured
#set
us-low
column7: [Xe] is 54 electrons and does not contain 4f, which first fills at Z=58; [Xe] 4f14 therefore asks for 68 electrons in an atom with Z=55. ld1.x counts a core of 60 and reports z_valence = 55 - 60 = -5, writing a UPF that no code can use. Upstream writes 4f-1 -- ld1's marker for an unoccupied test channel -- for this same element in the high set. Measured with QE 7.6 ld1.x: upstream gives z_valence=-5.00, 47 SCF iterations and "error in KS equations"; corrected gives z_valence=9.00 (5s2 5p6 6s1), 27 iterations, no warning, AE-PS eigenvalue agreement within 1e-5 Ry and transferability "excellent". The 4f channel is unoccupied and absent from the pseudo-wavefunction list, so the corrected deck is bit-for-bit identical to dropping 4f entirely.
